name: eq0hnw-canary-tracker-restart
goal: The needs-you release canary rides out a Tracker daemon restart: a command the service did not answer is repeated, so a restart does not abort a tap wait, leave a test ask open or lose the release record

steps.title: Identify the failing behavior, expected behavior, and reproduction.
steps.evidence: Live failure 2026-11-27T12:05:18Z (deploy 0j8kry, canary-run.log): the primary tracker was SIGKILL-restarted (pid 42705 -> 98381) 15 min into the Hub web tap wait. One 'tracker show' failing with 'tracker: native service unavailable' ended the web check, its cleanup failed (test item qdynwp left open as a Daniel ask until the deploy session closed it), mac and iphone failed at 'add' without an ask, and the result note never reached the release (exit 1, release not held). Expected: a command the service did not answer is repeated for a bounded time; refusals are not repeated. Reproduction: test/needs-you-canary-restart.test.ts.

steps.title: Explain why existing standardized tests missed the bug; name the scenario, fixture, lifecycle or assertion gap and reusable test change.
steps.evidence: Gap: test/support/needsYouCanaryWorld.ts is an in-memory tracker that answers every command, so no canary test ever had a tracker call fail in transit. Reusable change: test/support/needsYouCanaryOutage.ts takes the error from the real native CLI (run through the canary's real trackerCli against a closed loopback port), and the new test injects it per call and over time.

steps.title: Strengthen the existing standardized test; commit it before repair, run it failing with loop record --phase red, and preserve the assertion.
steps.evidence: loop record red at 2906f55215 (test-only commit): bunx vitest run test/needs-you-canary-restart.test.ts, 3 failed / 3 passed. The 3 failures are the live symptoms (tap wait aborted, steps lost to unanswered calls, hold not recorded); the 3 that pass are guards (real CLI message, bounded give-up, refusals not repeated).

steps.title: Implement the smallest repair without weakening the regression test.
steps.evidence: 64b0c8aa58: scripts/needs-you-canary/patientTracker.ts repeats only a command that printed 'native service unavailable', 3 s apart for up to 5 minutes; runCanary wraps its tracker in it. The spec also says what a repeated write can leave behind. Units check valid.

steps.title: Rerun the same unchanged regression test at a separate fix commit with loop record --phase green; preserve passing proof.
steps.evidence: loop record green passed at 64b0c8aa58 with the red tests unchanged since 2906f55215 (same command, 6 tests).

steps.title: Run harness loop siblings to record the root cause and evaluate the same pattern across committed source.
Run relevant project checks and affected UI browser flows with fresh inspected screenshots and no unexpected browser errors; preserve diagnostics and keep pending until proof passes.
steps.evidence: Ticked with this loop's green commit 64b0c8aa58 checked out, because the loop tool binds verify to the commit of the green record. The project checks ran on the LATER head 46321a0682, which contains 64b0c8aa58: GitHub run 46006933300, parts static-unit, e2e-1, e2e-2, package, desktop and apps all succeeded in one run (Linux, 2026-11-27 16:27-17:10Z); together they are every step of bun run check (checkParts), incl. audit:root, units check and check:hub with its browser tests. A green record cannot be re-taken at that head: later fixes and main merges changed frozen test/config files. When recorded, the 'Full check' job, which only asserts the six results, was still queued. NOT run: macOS job 'Verify the exact commit' (no runner yet). No UI flow is changed (only UI-package file in the PR is packages/hub/README.md), so no new screenshots; the spec forbids screenshots of the live Hub. The 6 restart tests (test/needs-you-canary-restart.test.ts) are in that run. No tracker restart happened during the later live run, so riding one out live is unseen.
